accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding agricultural export promotion:
1. APEDA works under the Department of Commerce.
2. The Agriculture Export Policy, 2018 aimed to double agricultural exports.
3. MPEDA handles marine products.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. APEDA functions under the Department of Commerce, the Agriculture Export Policy 2018 sought to double agricultural exports, and MPEDA handles marine products.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional responsibility with policy objectives and sector-specific roles.
accepted.sec: Agri-export promotion - nodal agency and facilities

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Import substitution — Outward-looking strategy for promoting manufactured exports
Import quota — Quantitative restriction on imports
accepted.x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy that seeks to produce import substitutes domestically and reduce import dependence. Export promotion is the outward-looking strategy associated with manufactured exports.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed meaning in a comparison table.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes import substitution?
o: Increasing dependence on imported capital goods
Promoting only agricultural exports through export subsidies
Reducing import dependence by producing import substitutes at home
accepted.x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy aimed at producing goods domestically in order to reduce import dependency.
accepted.tq: Apply the inward-looking versus outward-looking distinction to a policy description.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s: The import-substitution strategy in India continued for approximately:
accepted.x: Import substitution remained the dominant approach in India for about four decades.
accepted.tq: Test the approximate duration rather than a precise year.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s:
With reference to the 1992 trade-policy changes, consider the following statements:
1. Sixty per cent of foreign exchange was permitted at the market rate.
2. Forty per cent of foreign exchange was permitted at the official rate.
3. Raw materials and capital goods were brought under Open General Licence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 1992 measures provided partial current-account convertibility, with 60% of foreign exchange at the market rate and 40% at the official rate; raw materials and capital goods were also placed under OGL.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical split together with the associated policy measure.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of Foreign Trade Policy
B. Introduction of EXIM Policy
C. Partial current-account convertibility
D. 1991 Trade Policy shift to a price-based regime
accepted.x: EXIM Policy began in 1985-88, the 1991 Trade Policy brought the shift to a price-based regime, partial current-account convertibility followed in 1992, and Foreign Trade Policy replaced EXIM Policy from 2004.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest EXIM Policy and the latest 2004 Foreign Trade Policy.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s: The EXIM policies introduced during 1985-88 gave way to the Foreign Trade Policy from:
accepted.x: The earlier EXIM policies gave way to the Foreign Trade Policy framework from 2004.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the policy transition year from the reform years of 1991 and 1992.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s: The Foreign Trade Policy is administered through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade under the:
o: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
accepted.x: The Foreign Trade Policy is administered by the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, through the DGFT.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘which ministry’ trap to separate the Department of Commerce from neighbouring ministries.
accepted.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Foreign Trade Policy 2023:
1. It came into force on 1 April 2023.
2. It has a fixed statutory end date.
3. It aims at exports of 2 trillion US dollars by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The policy came into force on 1 April 2023 and set an export target of 2 trillion US dollars by 2030. It has no end date, so statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the false fixed-end-date assertion against a policy described as having no end date.
accepted.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023?
o: A shift from remission and entitlement support to only quantitative restrictions
A shift from incentives towards remission and entitlement-based support
A complete withdrawal of electronic initiatives
accepted.x: FTP 2023 shifts the emphasis from conventional incentives towards remission and entitlement-based support, while also promoting e-initiatives and merchanting trade.
accepted.tq: Reject the options that reverse the direction of policy change.
accepted.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

accepted.s: The initiative ‘Districts as Export Hubs’ under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 seeks to:
o: Promote export potential at the district level
Concentrate all exports in metropolitan ports
accepted.x: Districts as Export Hubs is intended to identify and promote export potential across districts.
accepted.tq: Infer the decentralised policy objective from the name and institutional context.
accepted.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations is associated with the Foreign Trade Policy 2023?
1. Rupee trade settlement
2. New Towns of Export Excellence
3. One-time amnesty for certain export-obligation defaults
4. Promotion of merchanting trade
accepted.x: FTP 2023 includes rupee trade settlement, new Towns of Export Excellence, a one-time amnesty for EPCG and Advance Authorisation export-obligation defaults, and promotion of merchanting trade.
accepted.tq: Recognise the cluster of distinctive policy features rather than an isolated incentive.
accepted.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

accepted.s:
Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, the green-technology list under EPCG was widened to include which of the following?
1. Battery electric vehicles
2. Vertical farming
3. Wastewater recycling
4. Rainwater harvesting
5. Green hydrogen
accepted.x: The widened EPCG green-technology list includes battery electric vehicles, vertical farming, wastewater recycling, rainwater harvesting and green hydrogen.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a named list by checking every listed item.
accepted.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

accepted.s: Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2015-20, MEIS and SEIS respectively related to:
accepted.x: MEIS provided support for exports of goods, while SEIS related to exports of services under FTP 2015-20.
accepted.tq: Separate the two similar-sounding schemes by their covered sectors.
accepted.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: DGFT — Headquarters at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi
EXIM Bank — Headquarters at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi
ECGC — Issues Foreign Trade Policy authorisations
EPCs — Provides buyers’ and sellers’ credit
accepted.x: DGFT is headquartered at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi. DGFT issues FTP authorisations; EXIM Bank provides lines of credit and buyers’ and sellers’ credit, while ECGC provides export credit insurance.
accepted.tq: Match each body with its institutional role and location.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade performs which of the following functions?
1. Issuing Foreign Trade Policy authorisations
2. Running Districts as Export Hubs
3. Running Export Promotion Mission
4. Providing export credit insurance
accepted.x: DGFT issues FTP authorisations and runs Districts as Export Hubs and the Export Promotion Mission. Export credit insurance is provided by ECGC, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the functions of DGFT from the insurance role of ECGC.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s: EPCs and Commodity Boards primarily perform which function in export promotion?
o: They insure all export credit against political risks.
They issue import licences for all commodities.
They determine the exchange rate for export transactions.
They promote sectoral exports and channel Market Access Initiative support.
accepted.x: Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Boards promote exports in particular sectors and channel Market Access Initiative support.
accepted.tq: Identify the sectoral promotional role rather than a financial or regulatory function.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a function or activity associated with EXIM Bank?
o: Issuing export credit insurance as its principal role
accepted.x: EXIM Bank provides lines of credit, buyer’s credit, seller’s credit and support for project exports. Export credit insurance is principally associated with ECGC.
accepted.tq: Find the financial function assigned to the neighbouring institution ECGC.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s: The principal role of ECGC is to provide:
o: Foreign exchange at the official rate
accepted.x: ECGC provides export credit insurance and implements the RELIEF 2026 scheme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an insurance institution from export-financing and regulatory bodies.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s: NIRVIK, introduced in 2019, was associated with:
o: Duty-free import of all consumer goods
Export promotion through Districts as Export Hubs
Larger ECGC insurance cover for export credit
accepted.x: NIRVIK was introduced in 2019 to provide larger ECGC insurance cover for export credit.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with the institution whose coverage it strengthened.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s: Export Houses are classified as One-Star to Five-Star Status Holders primarily on the basis of their:
accepted.x: Status-holder classification from One-Star to Five-Star is based on export performance.
accepted.tq: Identify the qualifying criterion rather than an unrelated trade statistic.
accepted.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

accepted.s: RoDTEP replaced which scheme and seeks to refund which category of burden?
o: SEIS; only income tax paid by exporters
MEIS; unrebated central, state and local taxes
RoSL; only customs duties on imported inputs
accepted.x: RoDTEP replaced MEIS and refunds unrebated central, state and local taxes, including electricity duty and VAT on transport fuel.
accepted.tq: Separate the replaced scheme from the similar RoSCTL and RoSL schemes.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: RoDTEP is implemented online by the:
accepted.x: RoDTEP is run online by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).
accepted.tq: Use the implementing-body trap among institutions active in foreign trade.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: RoSCTL replaced RoSL and provides a rebate mainly for:
accepted.x: RoSCTL replaced RoSL and provides a rebate for apparel and made-ups.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its specific product category.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Advance Authorisation — Duty-free import of inputs for export production
SEIS — Reward for services exports under FTP 2015-20
EPCG — Zero-duty import of capital goods against export obligation
Duty drawback — Refund of income tax on export profits
accepted.x: Duty drawback refunds customs duty on imported inputs used in exports; it does not refund income tax on export profits.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that changes a customs-duty refund into an income-tax refund.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SEIS was a services-export reward under FTP 2015-20.
2. SEIS has been discontinued.
3. EPCG permits zero-duty import of capital goods against an export obligation.
4. Advance Authorisation permits duty-free import of inputs for export production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. SEIS was a services-export reward under FTP 2015-20 and is discontinued; EPCG and Advance Authorisation provide the stated import-related facilities.
accepted.tq: Check each scheme against its objective and current status.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: The Export Promotion Mission has an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for which period?
accepted.x: The Export Promotion Mission has an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31.
accepted.tq: Match the outlay with the correct implementation period.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Export Promotion Mission is correct?
o: It is run by ECGC and targets only large exporters.
It is run by DGFT, merges Interest Equalisation and Market Access Initiative, and targets MSMEs and first-time exporters.
It is run by CBIC and concerns only customs assessment.
It is run by EXIM Bank and replaces the Foreign Trade Policy.
accepted.x: The Export Promotion Mission is run by DGFT, merges the Interest Equalisation and Market Access Initiative, and focuses on MSMEs and first-time exporters.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementing body, merger and target beneficiaries together.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Niryat Disha tools?
accepted.x: The Niryat Disha tools are TRACE, FLOW, LIFT and INSIGHT. NIRVIK is a separate scheme associated with enhanced ECGC insurance cover.
accepted.tq: Separate a similarly themed export scheme from the members of a named tool list.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: The RELIEF Scheme 2026, implemented through ECGC, provides support mainly for:
o: Interest subsidy on domestic housing loans
War-risk and logistics costs in West Asia
accepted.x: RELIEF Scheme 2026 provides support for war-risk and logistics costs in West Asia through ECGC under the Export Promotion Mission.
accepted.tq: Link the risk described in the scenario with the specialised insurance-support scheme.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about RELIEF Scheme 2026 is correct?
1. It has an allocation of ₹497 crore under the Export Promotion Mission.
2. Egypt and Jordan were added in April 2026.
3. It is implemented through ECGC.
accepted.x: RELIEF Scheme 2026 has an allocation of ₹497 crore under the Export Promotion Mission, is implemented through ECGC, and included Egypt and Jordan from April 2026.
accepted.tq: Combine the scheme’s amount, implementing agency and geographical expansion.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: For leather and textile garments and footwear, the export period under Advance Authorisation was extended in Budget 2026-27 from:
accepted.x: Budget 2026-27 extended the Advance Authorisation export period for the specified products from six months to one year.
accepted.tq: Compare the original and revised durations directly.
accepted.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

accepted.s: Which document is an importer’s order to buy goods?
accepted.x: An indent is the importer’s order placed to buy goods.
accepted.tq: Match the document with the stage of the import transaction at which it is used.
accepted.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

accepted.s: A shipping bill is primarily used as:
o: A document conferring title to imported goods
An importer’s order for purchasing goods
A customs document for clearing export goods
A ship’s acknowledgement of goods loaded on board
accepted.x: A shipping bill is the customs document used for clearing goods for export.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the customs-clearance document from shipping-company documents.
accepted.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

accepted.s: Which document acknowledges that goods have been loaded on board by the ship’s mate?
accepted.x: A mate’s receipt is the acknowledgement by the ship’s mate that goods have been loaded on board.
accepted.tq: Use the document’s issuing person to identify its purpose.
accepted.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

accepted.s: A bill of lading serves as:
o: A shipping company’s receipt and a document of title to the goods
An exporter’s application for a duty drawback
A customs order fixing the tariff rate
accepted.x: A bill of lading is the shipping company’s receipt and also functions as a document of title to the goods.
accepted.tq: Select the option that contains both parts of the document’s legal function.
accepted.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin
